problem:
Determine which of the following shaded regions depicts the domain of the vector field $F$ on ${R}^{2},$ given by

$$
F(x,y)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{y-x}}\,i+\sqrt{2-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}\,j\,.
$$
worked_solution:
The function $F$ can be expressed in terms of its components $P(x,y)$ and $Q(x,y)$ as

$$
F(x,y)=P(x,y)\,i+Q(x,y)\,j,
$$

where

$$
P(x,y)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{y-x}},\,Q(x,y)=\sqrt{2-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}.
$$

We first find the domain of each component function. Then, we compute their intersection to find the domain of $F:$

- The function $P(x,y)$ is defined when the expression under the radical is positive. So, to find the domain, we solve the following inequality:

$$
y-x>0\,⟹\,y>x.
$$

This defines the region ${D}_{1},$ shown below:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14042874/assets/c78759bc8f9926159065129e00c1fc8b4341ab83ad40cc87e67a2e82b3e6b089.png)

- The function $Q(x,y)$ is defined when the expression under the radical is positive or equal to zero. So, to find the domain, we solve the following inequality:

$$
2-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\ge 0\,⟹\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 2.
$$

This defines the region ${D}_{2},$ which is a circle of radius $\sqrt{2},$ as shown below:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14042874/assets/bdf02ff330f256327d0c9f1147c388b25184610b36ea7ab77bb2c570ec3be19a.png)

Finally, the domain $D$ of $F$ is given by ${D}_{1}\cap {D}_{2},$ shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14042874/assets/0d3180a60e33c05e904c8fc00fdec4197510198fef3de3fa8c7b3549609205f6.png)
